Subject: Escalator ramp proposal for Dedicated capacity (Aperture Health)

Hi Ellie —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a concise proposal that follows the "escalator" approach we discussed: an upfront prepay for Dedicated GPU capacity with predefined breakpoints where committed capacity steps up over the first 18 months. Key points in the attached PDF and the pricing workbook: 

- Proposal is structured as a 2-year commitment with an annual prepay option.
- Two discount bands: 15% term discount for 2-year prepay, 10% for annual prepay (paid up front).
- Escalator ramp (example): 30% of peak committed capacity in months 1–3, 60% by months 4–9, full commit by month 13.
- We suggested limited breakpoints (quarterly) and a 60-day notice window for adjustments to accommodate Aperture's seasonal traffic.
- Onboarding credit: one month of ramped capacity free (applied as usage credit).

I included an amortization view in the workbook so you can see how the prepay maps to monthly run-rate and unit cost. If you want, we can surface a counter with deeper early-year ramp (more front-loaded capacity) to match your Q1 product rollout.

Attachments: RI_EscalatorProposal_ApertureNov12.pdf (proposal), redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (scenarios).

Would you be up for a 30-minute call early next week to walk the options?

Thanks —
Monica

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Aperture ramp counter — proposed two-option response

Monica / team —

Thanks for the context. I've modelled two defensible commercial responses (attached pricing-scenarios-Aperture-Nov16.xlsx):

Option A (2-year full prepay, deeper term concession):
- 2-year upfront prepay, 20% term discount (applies to committed unit price).
- Escalator: 50% of peak in months 1–3, 80% by months 4–8, 100% by month 12.
- One mid-term "top-up" breakpoint after month 12 that allows Aperture to increase committed capacity at the then-current price (no retroactive price decrease).
- Limited scale-down flexibility: single permitted scale-down window at month 18 with 90-day notice; any scale-down triggers a pro-rated reconciliation and a breakage fee equal to 10% of the reduced capacity's remaining prepay amortization.
- Amortization schedule: monthly straight-line over 24 months; we provide the CSV for finance to ingest.
- Onboarding credit: 1 month free during ramp.

Option B (1-year annual prepay, modest concession):
- 1-year upfront prepay, 12% term discount.
- Escalator: 40% M1–M2, 75% by M6, 100% by M10.
- Flexible top-ups anytime; scale-downs require 60-day notice and are subject to standard reconciliation (no breakage fee).
- Amortization: monthly over 12 months.

Trade-offs / recommendation: Option A is heavily favored if they can commit to the 2-year prepay — the effective unit cost is materially lower and gives us predictable capacity planning. To get to 20% we should keep the breakpoint mechanics tight (single mid-term top-up, explicit breakage fee on scale-downs) and require a one-time non-refundable onboarding credit as part of the prepay.

Legal flags: we should run the "breakage fee" and "scale-down reconciliation" language by legal; we need to ensure the audit and instance-level logs clause is supported by Private/Dedicated telemetry policy.

I attached the scenario workbook and a short amortization CSV. If Monica wants, I can take the call with Aperture and walk through the numbers.

-Aditya

Attachments: pricing-scenarios-Aperture-Nov16.xlsx
